fact_text: Markets should be compared over long horizons, since short-run volatility and starting valuations distort shorter comparisons while business profit growth dominates over decades.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The start date of a cross-market comparison changes the result: at July 2001 the US indices were already hit by the dot-com bust, while the PSX had already rallied about 50% from its 1999 level.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Measured in US dollars from July 2001 to 2026, the analyst's calculation has PSX returning about 28 times the starting value, well ahead of the US indices he compared it with.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Much of PSX's rupee gain since 2001 is eroded by rupee depreciation: the dollar rose from about 55 to about 280 rupees over the same period.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst attributes PSX's superior dollar returns to Pakistani business owners earning high profits on capital despite high interest and tax rates, and calls this alpha or better planning.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX suffers drawdowns of 30 to 50% in boom-bust cycles, as in the 2007 fall and the 2017 to 2020 slide into COVID, comparable in size to US drawdowns of the same kind.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Pakistan valuations de-rate while the index is falling, so dollar returns can fall harder than rupee returns, because currency loss compounds the equity drop for dollar-based investors.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst names reserves, interest rates and political stability as the main drivers of PSX boom-bust cycles and recommends tracking them on a simple dashboard.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX bull phases have historically delivered about 30% a year on average, because profits grow and valuations do not compress during the upswing, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the past 25 years only a few US years delivered about 35% dollar returns, which the analyst uses to argue that PSX bull phases are the stronger opportunity for Pakistani investors.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's illustrative bull-phase framework is roughly 40 to 50% in PSX, 10 to 15% in international stocks and the rest in gold, with money needed within two to three years held in fixed income.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When a bust cycle with valuation falls is expected, the analyst shifts the bias toward gold, and returns to PSX when the bull framework switches back on.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Overseas Pakistanis can repatriate dollars from local investments at the chosen time, which the analyst says reduces the risk of capital being trapped in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Listed stocks in Pakistan tend to beat inflation because business owners pass cost increases into prices, so company profits and share prices keep pace with or exceed inflation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Long-run research on asset classes, which the analyst cites, finds equities beat most other classes such as bonds, cash and art in real terms, with business profits as the reason.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For planning, the analyst uses a 17% average PSX return, based on decades of history and about 18% long-run growth in listed company profits, rather than recent short-run averages.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Advisers can distort return assumptions by quoting low averages or picking bad years, so the analyst treats 25 to 30 year averages as the honest benchmark for stock returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank deposits and savings schemes in Pakistan pay only slightly above or below inflation before tax, and fixed-income returns face higher tax than the equity rate the analyst cites, so they rarely build wealth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's long-run inflation has averaged roughly 9 to 10% a year, the analyst notes, which sets the real-return hurdle for any savings or SIP plan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A SIP judged in real terms must raise its monthly contribution each year by the inflation rate; otherwise later contributions are worth less in real terms and the plan overstates its result.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Buying a stock on consecutive upper-circuit days and selling at the first lower circuit is judged unreliable, because the next day's move is uncertain and a lower circuit can trap sellers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For deep-value small or mid-cap stocks the analyst keeps the position small, not more than about 5% of the portfolio, and waits from six months to two years for the price to converge to fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Before buying a cheap stock, check that its fair value is not eroding through losses or debt, since two years of losses can cut fair value sharply and turn a bargain into a trap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's reserves rule of thumb: about three months of import cover is a comfortable level, and a fall of 15 to 20% from a reserves peak near 20 billion USD is a cue to check whether a bust cycle has started.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst links the cut in the super tax in Budget 2026 to higher listed company profits, and treats that as a support for the market outlook.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PSX moved sideways in early 2025, then rallied from July 2025 after the India-Pakistan conflict improved Pakistan's geopolitical position and interest rates fell; the analyst sees a similar pattern as possible.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sugar mills can trade far below replacement cost, since building a new crushing plant costs several times what an established mill of the same capacity is valued at in the market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sugar sector stocks are often misvalued because few investors follow them, so cheap entries appear, but the analyst warns that not every stock trades near fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's sugar mill case: a debt-free mill that was not making losses traded far below a normal mill's value, so he bought a small position and waited for the market cap to converge.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For that deep-value holding the analyst's own exit approach was to sell as the market cap approached the value of a normal mill, rather than trade on daily price moves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's first investment was a medium-cap version of a small cement company, with no debt and no losses, bought at a low price relative to its fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lump-sum buying suits a stock the investor believes is deeply undervalued and will re-rate within one to two years, while SIP suits quality companies held over many years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When a SIP holding reaches fair value, the analyst keeps investing only if the company is high quality with a clean record and no visible risks; a medium-quality stock bought cheap and now at fair value should be sold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: New investors are advised to commit only part of planned capital at first, for example half, and add later after watching a full boom-bust cycle build conviction.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ghani Chemical's JVs with OGDC and Mari show oil and gas companies using its plants for carbon-reduction and waste-gas projects, which the analyst expects could extend to other oil and gas fields.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ghani Chemical's JV with Mari for a gas-related plant is expected to come online around FY29, adding roughly PKR 1.5 per share to earnings at the analyst's assumed early utilisation of 60 to 70%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ghani Chemical has a five-year CNG-related contract with OGDC, which the analyst expects to lift earnings per share once the project is online.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ghani Chemical's new plant sits in a tax-free zone, so extra profit from growth or higher gas prices escapes the 40% corporate tax rate the analyst cites.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oxygen output from Ghani Chemical could find demand if shipbreaking restarts, or add profit if oxygen prices rise, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Joint ventures with larger companies can raise investor trust in a mid-sized company, lifting the P/E multiple investors pay; the analyst cites Tariq Glass's glass-plant JVs with ICI and Lucky Core.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gandhara Automobiles' 2025 earnings were lifted by a launch-driven surge in JAC T9 pickup bookings and deliveries, but demand later softened and dealers began offering discounts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gandhara's trailing P/E can look misleadingly low because first-half FY26 earnings were boosted by unusually high imported-truck sales that later normalised, so past earnings may not repeat.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Competition in the pickup segment is rising, and a new model from Gandhara's JAC partner could open a new business line, which the analyst says investors should watch.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst views Gandhara's JAC partnership as a strength because the partner's global product portfolio supports future model launches.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PSX vs US Stocks: Which Market Can Build More Wealth?' (YouTube transcript, undated)
